Subject: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift & SLA mapping (Cumulus Retail)

Hi Leah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on the Q4 projections your team shared, we recommend a staged commit uplift to avoid soft-throttles during peak flash sales. High level proposal: increase hosted API monthly commit from 500M tokens to 1.2B tokens, 12-month term, with a committed discount of 22% off standard hosted rates and a burst pocket for 200M tokens at a slightly elevated rate.

I've attached a mutual action plan (MAP) and an ops checklist for provisioning. Key asks before we finalize:
- Procurement sign-off on the 12-month term and billing schedule
- Confirmation of the Q4 traffic window (expected peak dates)
- Legal review for small SLA amendment (guaranteed 99.9% uptime for production routes)

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share the MAP and a DocuSign package today for signature.
2) Karthik / Marissa will coordinate provisioning timeline and run a quick capacity smoke test on staging.
3) Procurement provides PO or signed DocuSign within 7 business days for an effective June 1 start.

Attachments: Cumulus_MAP_Q3-Q4_2028.xlsx (MAP), draft DocuSign (PDF stub)

If that plan looks good I’ll send the DocuSign link and onboarding calendar invite.

Best,

Great questions — answers below and I’ve embedded the operational bits for your procurement and infra teams. Quoted original for context.

On Wed, May 15, 2028 at 11:03 AM Leah Chen <leah@cumulusretail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we move to signatures:
>
> 1) Can you confirm the per-token effective rate after the 22% committed discount and whether embeddings are included or billed separately?
> 2) We have a hard cap requirement for test environments to prevent accidental cost overruns — can staging be isolated with separate quota and telemetry?
> 3) For the burst pocket: is it first-come billing (consumes burst then falls back) or a parallel bucket? We need to map to our internal alerting.

Answers / details:
- Effective rates: post-discount effective hosted generation rate = $0.0009 per token (generation). Embeddings are billed separately at $0.0012 per embedding unit; we can include an estimated monthly embeddings baseline in the MAP if helpful.
- Staging isolation: yes — we provision a separate API key + project with its own quota and alert rules. We will mark staging tags in telemetry and exclude from production billing.
- Burst pocket mechanics: parallel bucket model. Production consumes committed bucket first; if production throughput exceeds commit, it consumes from the burst pocket. Burst consumption shows up separately in billing and in the console under "burst usage" so you can configure alerts per-bucket.

Proposed MAP highlights (attached):
- Month 1 (June): Provisioning + traffic smoke test, 25% traffic routed from canary to production.
- Month 2-3: Gradual ramp to 75% of expected Q4 traffic, observability checks and quality evals.
- Month 4 onward: Full ramp; burst pocket available for unanticipated peaks.

Deliverables I’ll attach to DocuSign: MAP (spreadsheet), SOW stub (1 page), and the amendment for the committed rates/SLA.

Would you like me to include an itemized billing sample for your procurement pack? I can generate a 12-month amortized invoice view.

Best,
Stephanie
